circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, designed by Hermann Tilke, is a 5. 281-kilometre track located on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island that has served as the venue for Formula One's season-closing Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street racing venue positioned around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, holding an FIA Grade 1 classification. It serves as the permanent home of the Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various supporting championships and races held there annually.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Situated in Spielberg, Styria, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit initially operated as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix continuously between 1970 and 1987. Following modifications and a rebranding to the A1-Ring, it resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital city, situated along Baku Boulevard with a lap distance of 6. 003 km, ranking it as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the maiden Formula One Grand Prix held in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other racing series. The venue, holding FIA Grade 1 status, has accommodated various motorsport events including drag racing, endurance competitions, and a brief period of V8 Supercar racing from 2006 to 2010, while offering multiple circuit configurations for different racing categories.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner complexities, making it suitable for testing various racing skills. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Spa-Francorchamps circuit in Belgium is a 7. 004 km track that has hosted Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured in the championship's inaugural season. The venue has maintained continuous Belgian Grand Prix appearances annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary racing facility that annually hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its primary use for Formula One, the track has served as a venue for multiple international motorsport series, including sports car championships and various North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility served as the home of the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix during two separate periods, initially from 2004 through 2019 before returning from 2024 onwards. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include additional international competitions alongside its flagship Grand Prix event.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, a racing venue located in England near Northamptonshire, became the inaugural host of the British Grand Prix in 1948 and staged the opening race of the Formula One World Championship in 1950. The circuit shared hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch for three decades before becoming the permanent home of Britain's Grand Prix from 1987 onward, while also serving as a venue for international motorcycle racing.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest became the first Formula One circuit in Eastern Europe when it hosted its inaugural Grand Prix in 1986, constructed in just eight months, a record for F1 track building. Located in Mogyoród outside the capital rather than in the city's main park as originally planned, the 4. 381 km circuit has since become a permanent fixture on the championship calendar.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza near Milan is a 5. 793 km circuit established in 1922 as Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue, renowned as "the Temple of Speed" for its fast straights and sweeping bends. Since 1949, it has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix, making it one of the few circuits to feature on the Formula One calendar throughout the sport's history, with only a brief closure in 1980 for renovation.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland in Mie Prefecture, hosting a capacity of 155,000 spectators. The track is primarily renowned for staging both the Formula One World Championship and the Japanese Super Formula series.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course situated in Paradise, Nevada, that navigates through the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The track weaves past iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues, including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of motorsport's most visually distinctive venues.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 304 km Mexico City circuit is named after two brothers who died racing, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez. The track returned to hosting Formula One in 2015 after a 23-year absence, though on a different layout than during its previous hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it became home to the Miami Grand Prix when the event joined the championship calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street course that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the waterfront of Monaco's harbour. Though technically spanning multiple neighbourhoods, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its primary location within the Monte Carlo area.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch dunes near Amsterdam and the North Sea, this 4. 259 km venue hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its 2021 return to the Formula One calendar after a lengthy absence. The partnership concluded in 2026, marking the end of the circuit's tenure in the sport's premier racing series.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a motor racing venue positioned north of Doha in Qatar, featuring a 5. 419 km layout with a notably long 1. 068 km main straight and holding FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Brazil's Interlagos circuit, spanning 4. 309 kilometers near São Paulo, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late racing driver José Carlos Pace. The counterclockwise track has hosted Formula One racing and features an adjacent kart facility bearing Ayrton Senna's name.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track positioned along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021. The venue also began accommodating Formula E racing in 2025, establishing itself as a multi-series motorsport destination.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary racing layout that winds through Singapore's Marina Bay district, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang neighborhoods.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One machinery. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility in Austin, Texas that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international racing events including MotoGP's Americas round and various endurance racing championships, while having previously accommodated numerous other series including IndyCar and rallycross competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand in the sport.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world championships during his 23-season career with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours wins and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the only driver to win both the F1 and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes on the Formula One grid in 2025 and has already secured eight Grand Prix victories during his early career in the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian racing driver Gabi Bortoleto currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after a lengthy career spanning 13 seasons. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while with Mercedes during 2019 and 2020, accumulating 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport driver currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve position with Haas while competing in European endurance racing with Nielsen Racing in the LMP2 category. He has made limited Formula One appearances, taking part in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved a grand prix victory at Monza in 2020 while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, representing France in Formula One, races for Red Bull Racing and holds both French and Algerian nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple performance records in the sport, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in Formula One history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi and has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, including a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver has competed for Ferrari across nine seasons, securing nine Grand Prix victories and finishing as championship runner-up in 2022. Leclerc continues to race for the Italian marque in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also racing part-time in NASCAR for Trackhouse Racing. He previously competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and returning in 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, where he secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship. The accomplished competitor has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One for Haas. The driver achieved a Grand Prix victory in 2021 while driving for Alpine, specifically at the Hungarian round of that season.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Sergio Pérez, a Mexican driver, currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after finishing second in the 2023 drivers' championship while with Red Bull. Throughout his 15-season career, Pérez has claimed six Grand Prix victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his time in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell competes for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz has established himself in Formula One over 12 seasons, securing four Grand Prix victories throughout his career. He currently races for Williams in the championship.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with Proton Competition in the LMGT3 category. Following a two-season Formula One stint from 2023 to 2024, he has transitioned to sportscar racing, previously competing in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver competing in Formula One, currently racing for Aston Martin.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently holding a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. After competing as a full-time Formula One participant from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a supporting role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch driver Max Verstappen has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championship titles with Red Bull Racing from 2021 through 2024, establishing himself as a dominant force in the sport with 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver currently holding a reserve role with Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top category from 2022 through 2024, establishing himself as the sole Chinese driver to have participated in Formula One competition.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated as Renault's official Formula One outfit from 2021 onwards under the Alpine brand banner, following a rebranding that highlighted the French manufacturer's sports car division. After more than two decades as Renault's works team, the squad ended its factory partnership when the company withdrew from the sport at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through multiple incarnations as a British manufacturer, with the current operation run by AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari, stands as the most decorated and longest-running Formula One team, participating in every World Championship since the sport's inaugural season in 1950. Nicknamed "the Prancing Horse" after their distinctive emblem, the team has established an unmatched legacy of success throughout the championship's seven-decade history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas founded this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the squad entering the sport in 2016. Ayao Komatsu currently leads the team as principal, taking over from Guenther Steiner, who held the position since the team's establishment before departing in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm initially excelled in endurance racing before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. After competing continuously for over three decades, the team concluded its F1 operations in 2025 as one of the championship's longest-serving constructor entries before being acquired by Audi to form the foundation of its works team.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under sponsorship arrangements. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group structure, with ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and power unit supplier, with the current team operating from Brackley under a German licence. In 2022, ownership was restructured to include equal stakes held by Mercedes-Benz Group, team principal Toto Wolff, and Ineos alongside the existing partnership with Petronas. The team is traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows" due to its historic Mercedes racing identity.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as the second team within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a supporting facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's expansion strategy in the sport through a dual-team structure.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned constructors alongside Red Bull Racing, the squad operates from Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, based in England under an Austrian racing licence, emerged as a Formula One competitor in 2005 and has since become one of two top-tier teams within the Red Bull GmbH motorsport portfolio. Led by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade tenure before his 2025 departure, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as its new leadership figure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, operating as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. The team is headquartered at its Grove, Oxfordshire facility, which spans 60 acres and serves as both its design and manufacturing base.
